judged_text: A token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a `prisma.credential.update` now runs unconditionally on every SalesforceCalendarService construction, with no expiry check, where previously the service constructed its connection without any remote call. Every calendar operation touching Salesforce (availability checks, booking flows) pays a synchronous remote token-refresh round trip and a credential DB write, multiplying load on the Salesforce token endpoint and risking throttling/bans that turn into booking-path failures; the guarded refresh the expiry timestamp exists for was replaced by an unconditional one.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, a refresh-token request to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` is now executed before creating the `jsforce.Connection`, followed by `await prisma.credential.update(...)`, with no conditional guard/expiry check shown in the diff. This means constructing/initializing the service will always incur a remote round-trip plus a DB write, which is a concrete perf/operational concern (rate limiting/throttling risk) grounded in the added code, even if it may not be a strict functional correctness defect.
